summary: For ages 7–9, teach wind as a consequence of uneven solar heating: the Sun heats Earth's surface unevenly, warm air is lighter and rises, and cooler air flows in to take its place — that moving air IS the wind. Anchor to the sea breeze (land heats faster than sea) as the canonical concrete example, make the invisible air visible through its effects (streamers, smoke, a pinwheel), and teach the full causal chain rather than a single fact. Confront the common belief that wind is 'made by' trees or waves, or that it is a special substance separate from air.
misconceptions: Wind is made by trees swaying, waves, or fans — those show or move air but the driver is uneven heating
Wind 'comes from' a fixed place or is a substance stored somewhere, rather than air flowing to replace risen warm air
Warm air sinks / cold air rises (reversed) — warm air is lighter and rises
Wind and the air are different things — wind IS moving air
Heating happens evenly, so there'd be no reason for air to move

activities.title: Sea-breeze convection playground
steps: Look at a cross-section showing the Sun, warm land, cool sea, and the air above
Warm the land using a Sun/heat control and watch a column of warm air rise over the land
Watch streamers (or smoke traces) reveal cooler sea air streaming sideways to fill the gap left by the risen warm air — and name that sideways flow as the wind
Turn the heat UP and observe the breeze strengthen; turn it DOWN and watch the breeze die away
Switch to a cool night where the land cools faster than the sea, and observe the breeze reverse direction; explain why
activities.insight: Wind is not a mysterious push and is not made by trees or waves — it is simply air moving to replace warm air that rose because the Sun heated the surface unevenly. Changing the heating changes the wind; removing the uneven heating stops it.

activities.title: Make the invisible air visible
steps: Use streamers, smoke traces, or a pinwheel to detect moving air you cannot see
Observe which way the indicators point and describe the direction and strength of the air movement
Relate what the indicators show back to warm air rising somewhere and cooler air flowing in
activities.insight: Air itself is invisible, but its movement can be detected through its effects — and those effects are evidence of air flowing, which is what wind is.

activities.title: Order the causal chain and explain the sea breeze
steps: Arrange the steps of the causal chain in order: uneven heating → warm air rises → cooler air moves in → wind
In your own words, explain why a breeze often blows from the sea onto the land on a hot afternoon
Predict and explain which way the breeze blows at night when the land cools faster than the sea
Decide whether there could be wind over the open ocean with no trees or hills, and say what causes it
activities.insight: The learner can state and apply the full chain of causes, not just recite that wind exists, and can use it to predict wind direction in new situations.

activities.title: Ask a weather expert why the wind blows
steps: Pose the question 'why does the wind blow?' and listen to or read an explanation that narrates uneven heating, rising warm air, and cooler air moving in
Retell the chain back and ask a follow-up, such as what would happen if the Sun heated everywhere equally
activities.insight: The same causal chain can be put into words and reasoned about in dialogue, reinforcing the explanation the learner has observed.

checkQuestion: At the seaside on a hot afternoon a breeze often blows in from the sea onto the land. What makes the air move — what is wind, really?
checkAnswer: The Sun heats the land more than the sea; air over the warm land warms, becomes lighter and rises; cooler, denser air from over the sea flows in to take its place — that moving air is the wind. Wind is air moving because of uneven heating, from cooler/denser toward warmer/rising air.
